examples.ko: 동생이 엄마한테 제 비밀을 다 고해바쳤어요.
examples.en: My little brother snitched all my secrets to Mom.
I wonder who told on us to the teacher.

examples.ko: 친구가 고해바칠까 봐 걱정돼서 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was afraid my friend would tell on me, so I couldn't say anything.
People who tattle aren't popular with their friends.

examples.ko: 언니한테 고해바쳐도 소용없어요, 제가 먼저 말할 거예요.
examples.en: Telling my sister is pointless; I'll tell her first.
I'm really disappointed that you secretly told on your friend.

explain: '일러바치다', '고자질하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 남의 잘못을 윗사람에게 몰래 말하는 것이라서 말하는 사람을 비난하는 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '일러바치다'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '일러바치다' and '고자질하다'. Since it means secretly telling someone in authority about another person's fault, it carries a tone of blame toward the teller. In everyday talk '일러바치다' is also common.

en: to play a joke on; to play a trick on

examples.ko: 형이 자꾸 저를 골려서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: My older brother keeps teasing me, and I got angry.
My friends played a trick on me at the birthday party.

examples.ko: 동생을 골리지 말고 같이 놀아 주세요.
examples.en: Don't tease your little brother, play with him.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 학생들을 골리는 것을 좋아하세요.
examples.en: That teacher likes to tease his students.

examples.ko: 장난으로 골렸는데 진짜 화낼 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was just teasing, but I didn't think he would get really angry.

examples.ko: 친구를 골려 주려고 가짜 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote a fake letter to play a trick on my friend.

explain: '놀리다'와 비슷하지만 일부러 약을 올려서 상대를 당황하거나 화나게 만든다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 반드시 '~를 골리다'처럼 대상이 필요해요. 정도가 심하면 괴롭힘처럼 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '놀리다', but it feels more like deliberately provoking someone to fluster or annoy them. It always needs an object, as in '~를 골리다'. If it goes too far, it can sound like bullying.

examples.en: In front of my mother, my father becomes henpecked.
My friends tease me by calling me henpecked.
I watched a comedy with a henpecked husband in it.

examples.ko: 그는 겉으로는 센 척해도 사실 공처가예요.
examples.en: He acts tough on the outside, but he is actually henpecked.

examples.ko: 공처가 소리를 들어도 우리 집은 평화로워요.
examples.en: Even if I'm called henpecked, our home is peaceful.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 소문난 공처가라서 늘 일찍 집에 가요.
examples.en: My uncle is a well-known henpecked husband, so he always goes home early.

explain: 아내를 몹시 무서워하거나 아내 말을 잘 따르는 남편을 조금 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 반대로 아내를 많이 사랑하는 남편은 '애처가'라고 해요. 본인에게 쓰면 농담이 되지만 남에게 직접 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a teasing word for a husband who is very afraid of his wife or does what she says. A husband who loves his wife a lot is called '애처가', the contrasting word. Using it about yourself can be a joke, but saying it directly to someone else can be rude.

en: to be freaky; to be bad-tempered

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 성격이 좀 괴팍하셔서 말을 걸기 어려워요.
examples.en: My grandfather is a bit cranky, so it's hard to talk to him.
That professor is eccentric, but he cares about his students.

examples.ko: 괴팍한 취미를 가진 사람이 우리 동네에 살아요.
examples.en: A person with an eccentric hobby lives in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 성미가 괴팍해지는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people become more cranky as they get older.
That writer is famous for being eccentric.

examples.ko: 제 상사는 괴팍해서 기분을 맞추기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: My boss is so cranky that it's hard to keep him happy.

explain: 주로 사람의 성격이나 성미, 취미가 까다롭고 별나서 맞추기 어렵다는 느낌일 때 써요. 윗사람에게 쓸 때는 '괴팍하시다'처럼 '-시-'를 넣어요. 단순히 재미있게 특이한 사람은 '독특하다'나 '특이하다'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for a person's temperament or hobbies when they are fussy and peculiar and hard to deal with. For someone older or senior, add '-시-', as in '괴팍하시다'. For someone who is simply interestingly unusual, '독특하다' or '특이하다' fits better.

en: to coax; to talk someone into

examples.ko: 동생이 아빠를 구워삶아서 용돈을 받아 냈어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling sweet-talked Dad into giving pocket money.
No matter how much I buttered her up, Mom didn't give permission.
He's an expert at buttering up his boss.
The salesperson kept complimenting the customer to win them over.

examples.ko: 친구를 구워삶아 숙제를 대신 시킬 생각이에요?
examples.en: Are you planning to sweet-talk your friend into doing your homework?
My older sister buttered me up, and I ended up giving in.

explain: 듣기 좋은 말이나 행동으로 상대를 내 뜻대로 움직이게 하는 느낌이에요. '구슬리다'와 비슷하지만 의도가 더 뻔히 보이고 약간 얄미운 뉘앙스가 있어요. 주로 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of steering someone your way with pleasant words or actions. It is similar to '구슬리다', but the intent is more obvious and it has a slightly sly, cheeky tone. It is mostly used in speech.

examples.ko: 사극에서 궁녀 역할을 맡은 배우가 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The actress who played a palace maid in the period drama became popular.

examples.ko: 조선 시대 궁녀들은 왕과 왕비를 가까이에서 모셨어요.
examples.en: Palace women in the Joseon era served the king and queen up close.

examples.ko: 궁녀가 되면 평생 궁궐 밖으로 나가기 어려웠대요.
examples.en: I heard that once you became a palace maid, it was hard to leave the palace for life.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 궁녀의 옷차림을 재현한 전시를 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum I saw an exhibit recreating a palace maid's clothing.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 궁녀는 왕의 비밀을 알아내고 몹시 놀라요.
examples.en: The palace maid in the drama finds out the king's secret and is shocked.

examples.ko: 궁녀들이 궁궐 마당을 바쁘게 오가는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene where palace maids hurry back and forth across the palace yard.

explain: 궁궐에서 일하던 여성을 가리키는 말이라 사극이나 역사 이야기에서 자주 들어요. 사극에서는 '상궁', '나인' 같은 말도 같이 나오니 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 지금은 쓰지 않는 역사 속 신분이에요.
explain_en: It refers to women who worked in the royal palace, so you hear it often in period dramas and history stories. Words like '상궁' and '나인' also appear in those dramas, so it helps to learn them together. It is a historical status that no longer exists today.

examples.en: The doctor advised me to exercise.

examples.ko: 친구가 같이 여행 가자고 권유해서 가게 됐어요.
examples.en: A friend invited me on a trip, so I ended up going.

examples.ko: 점원이 새 상품을 계속 권유해서 부담스러웠어요.
examples.en: The clerk kept pushing new products, and it felt like pressure.
The teacher encourages students to read books.
I won't force you to do it.
My parents urged me to study abroad.

explain: 상대가 어떤 일을 해 보도록 부드럽게 이끌 때 써요. '추천하다'는 좋은 것을 알려 주는 느낌이고, '권유하다'는 행동하도록 마음을 움직이는 느낌이에요. 강하게 시키면 '강요하다'예요.
explain_en: Used when gently steering someone toward doing something. '추천하다' is about pointing out something good; '권유하다' is about moving the person to act. Pushing hard is '강요하다' (force).

examples.en: I fell for my friend's coaxing and skipped class.
That sweet temptation was actually a lie.

examples.ko: 아이들은 어른의 꼬임을 쉽게 알아채지 못해요.
examples.en: Children can't easily notice an adult's enticement.

examples.ko: 누구의 꼬임으로 이런 일을 했는지 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Tell me whose enticement led you to do this.
Enticement sounds like nice words at first.

examples.ko: 그 광고의 꼬임 때문에 필요 없는 물건을 샀어요.
examples.en: That ad tempted me into buying something I didn't need.

explain: '꼬임에 넘어가다', '꼬임에 빠지다'처럼 짝말로 외워 두면 편해요. 동사는 '꼬드기다'이고, 일상 대화에서는 '꼬시다'라고도 해요. 같은 글자의 '꼬임'이 실이나 줄이 꼬인 상태를 가리킬 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is easiest to learn as a set phrase, like '꼬임에 넘어가다' or '꼬임에 빠지다'. The related verb is '꼬드기다', and in everyday talk people also say '꼬시다'. The same word '꼬임' can also mean the state of a thread or rope being twisted.

examples.en: My father lived his whole life as a farmer.

examples.ko: 저 농사꾼 아저씨는 일 솜씨가 대단해요.
examples.en: That farmer uncle is really skilled at his work.
A farmer's hands are rough but warm.
I also want to become a farmer someday.
He is from Seoul but works like a farmer.
Farmers can't help being sensitive to the weather.

explain: 일상 대화에서 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 격식 있는 자리나 글에서는 '농부'나 '농민'이 더 무난해요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 잘하거나 즐겨 하는 사람 뒤에 붙는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a casual, everyday word. In formal settings or writing, '농부' or '농민' is safer. The suffix '-꾼' attaches to someone who does a particular job or does it habitually.

examples.en: My younger sibling slyly pretended not to know.

examples.ko: 능청맞은 얼굴로 거짓말을 해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was shocked that he lied with such a straight face.

examples.ko: 어쩜 그렇게 능청맞아요? 하나도 안 떨리나 봐요.
examples.en: How can you be so brazen? You don't seem nervous at all.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 능청맞아서 누구도 화를 내지 못해요.
examples.en: That child is so cheeky that no one can get angry at him.
My usually sly friend spoke honestly today.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 생각보다 능청맞지 않아서 금방 들켰어요.
examples.en: He wasn't as cunning as I thought, so he got caught right away.

explain: '능청스럽다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는데, 조금 더 구어체 느낌이에요. 모르는 척하는 태도를 얄밉거나 재미있게 볼 때 써요. 활용은 '능청맞아요, 능청맞은, 능청맞게'처럼 규칙적이에요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '능청스럽다' but feels a little more colloquial. You use it when you see someone's feigned innocence as cheeky or amusing. It conjugates regularly: '능청맞아요, 능청맞은, 능청맞게'.

en: good handwriting; person with good penmanship

examples.en: The teacher is famous for beautiful handwriting.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 글씨를 잘 써서 달필이에요.
examples.en: That friend writes very well; he has fine handwriting.

examples.ko: 달필인 사람이 쓴 편지는 읽기도 좋아요.
examples.en: A letter written by someone with fine handwriting is pleasant to read.

examples.ko: 아버지는 달필이라서 축하 글을 자주 부탁받으세요.
examples.en: My father has fine handwriting, so he is often asked to write congratulatory messages.

examples.ko: 저는 달필은 아니지만 또박또박 쓰려고 해요.
examples.en: I don't have fine handwriting, but I try to write neatly.

examples.ko: 달필이 아니어도 정성이 담긴 카드는 좋아요.
examples.en: Even without fine handwriting, a card written with care is lovely.

explain: 글씨를 잘 쓰는 것, 또는 그런 사람을 말해요. 반대말은 '악필'이에요. 보통 대화에서는 '글씨를 잘 쓰다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to writing well by hand, or to a person who does. Its opposite is '악필' (poor handwriting). In ordinary conversation people more often say '글씨를 잘 쓰다'.

examples.en: My father works with vigor like a true man.
Keep your promises like a real man.

examples.ko: 그 정도 일에 우는 건 대장부가 할 짓이 아니에요.
examples.en: Crying over something like that is not what a real man does.
My grandmother was a woman, but people called her bold and big-hearted like a real man.

examples.ko: 내가 대장부라면 이 일을 반드시 해낼 거예요.
examples.en: If I were a real man, I would surely pull this off.
He overcame the hardship with the spirit of a stout-hearted man.

explain: 씩씩하고 마음이 넓고 당당한 남자를 가리키는 옛 느낌의 말이에요. 요즘은 성격이 시원시원한 여성에게 '대장부 같다'고도 하고, '여장부'라는 말도 있어요. 칭찬으로 쓰지만 성별 틀을 담은 말이라 쓸 때 조심하는 사람도 있어요.
explain_en: It is an old-fashioned word for a manly man who is spirited, broad-hearted, and dignified. Today people also say '대장부 같다' about a frank, bold woman, and there is the word '여장부' too. It is meant as praise, but some people are careful with it because it carries gender expectations.

en: to be shrewd; to be impudent; to be wicked

examples.ko: 다섯 살짜리가 어른에게 따지다니 참 맹랑해요.
examples.en: A five-year-old arguing with an adult is quite cheeky.
Everyone laughed thanks to the cheeky little kid.

examples.ko: 어린아이가 말을 어찌나 맹랑하게 하는지 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised at how boldly the little child spoke.

examples.ko: 신입이 사장님께 먼저 악수를 청하다니 맹랑하네요.
examples.en: A new hire offering a handshake to the boss first is pretty bold.
That child was cheekier than he looked.
I scold him for being cheeky, but he's cute too.

explain: 주로 어린아이나 아랫사람이 나이에 비해 당돌하고 야무지게 굴 때 써요. 놀라움이 섞여 있어서 '당돌하다'와 비슷하지만 귀엽다는 느낌이 들 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when a child or junior person acts boldly and sharply beyond their age. It carries surprise, so it is similar to '당돌하다', and can sometimes feel endearing.

examples.ko: 저는 무남독녀라서 어릴 때부터 형제가 없어 심심했어요.
examples.en: I'm an only daughter, so I was bored as a kid with no siblings.

examples.ko: 그 집 무남독녀가 올해 대학에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The only daughter of that family got into university this year.

examples.ko: 무남독녀인 그녀는 부모님의 사랑을 듬뿍 받았어요.
examples.en: As an only daughter, she received plenty of love from her parents.
In the drama, the main character is the only daughter of a rich family.
How might a father feel marrying off his only daughter?

examples.ko: 무남독녀로 자라서 혼자 노는 데 익숙해요.
examples.en: I grew up as an only daughter, so I'm used to playing alone.

explain: 아들 없이 딸 하나만 있는 집의 외동딸을 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '외동딸'이 훨씬 자연스럽고, '무남독녀'는 드라마나 소설, 약간 옛날식 말투에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 딸 없이 아들 하나뿐이면 '무녀독남'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the only daughter in a family with no sons and no other children. In everyday speech '외동딸' is much more natural, while '무남독녀' shows up in dramas, novels and slightly old-fashioned speech. The counterpart for an only son with no sisters is '무녀독남'.

en: in minute detail; every little detail

examples.ko: 엄마가 어제 있었던 일을 미주알고주알 물어보셨어요.
examples.en: Mom asked about everything that happened yesterday in detail.

examples.ko: 친구는 데이트 이야기를 미주알고주알 다 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend told me every detail of her date.
Don't nitpick over every detail, just let it go.
Grandmother went on about every bit of neighborhood gossip.

examples.ko: 아이가 학교에서 있었던 일을 미주알고주알 이야기해요.
examples.en: The child tells me everything that happened at school.
The interviewer pried into everything, even my family.

explain: 사소한 것까지 하나하나 캐묻거나 낱낱이 말할 때 써요. '캐묻다', '따지다', '말하다' 같은 동사와 자주 같이 나와요. 귀찮거나 지나치다는 느낌이 들 때가 많아요.
explain_en: Use it when asking about or telling every small detail one by one. It often pairs with verbs like '캐묻다' (pry), '따지다' (nitpick) and '말하다' (tell). It often feels annoying or excessive.

examples.en: He disguised himself to avoid the police.
The kids dressed up as witches at the party.
Even if you disguise yourself, I know you from your voice.
The scene where the actor disguises himself as a grandmother was funny.
They say a celebrity came to the market in disguise.
She was disguised, so nobody recognized her.

explain: '변장하다'는 정체를 숨기거나 다른 사람처럼 보이려고 옷차림과 얼굴을 바꾸는 거예요. 배우가 역할에 맞게 꾸미는 건 '분장'이라고 해요. '변장'은 누군가를 속이거나 알아보지 못하게 하려는 목적이 있을 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: 변장하다 means changing your clothes and face to hide who you are or pass as someone else. When an actor is made up for a role, the word is 분장. 변장 fits best when the aim is to fool people or avoid being recognized.

examples.en: I moved out of my parents' home when I got married.
My younger sibling also plans to move out soon.

examples.ko: 아들이 직장 때문에 분가해서 따로 살아요.
examples.en: My son moved out because of his job and lives separately.
My uncle moved out a long time ago.
When would be a good time to move out?

examples.ko: 우리 부부는 아이가 태어나기 전에 분가해요.
examples.en: My spouse and I are moving out before the baby is born.

explain: 주로 결혼한 자녀가 부모님 집에서 나와 따로 사는 경우에 써서, 혼자 사는 '자취하다'와는 느낌이 달라요. 높이면 '분가하셨어요'라고 하고, 반대말은 '합가하다'예요. 요즘 대화에서는 '독립하다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when a married child leaves the parents' home to live separately, which feels different from '자취하다' (living alone). The honorific form is '분가하셨어요', and the opposite is '합가하다'. In conversation today '독립하다' is also very common.

en: to sponge off; to mooch off

examples.ko: 그는 친구 집에 빌붙어 몇 달째 살고 있어요.
examples.en: He has been mooching off his friend's place for months now.

examples.ko: 남에게 빌붙지 말고 스스로 일해서 살아요.
examples.en: Don't sponge off others; work and live on your own.

examples.ko: 부잣집에 빌붙어서 편하게 지내려는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who try to live comfortably by clinging to a rich family.
My younger brother, who used to mooch off his older brother, finally got a job.

examples.ko: 권력자에게 빌붙는 사람들을 저는 좋아하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't like people who suck up to those in power.
How long are you going to keep living off your parents?

explain: '얹혀살다'는 남의 집에서 신세 지며 사는 것 자체를 말하는 반면, '빌붙다'는 이익을 챙기려고 달라붙는 나쁜 느낌이 더 강해요. 돈이나 힘 있는 사람에게 기대어 사는 사람에게 쓰기 때문에, 앞에 있는 사람에게 말하면 모욕이 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: '얹혀살다' simply describes living at someone else's expense, while '빌붙다' carries a stronger negative sense of clinging on to gain benefits. It is used for people who lean on those with money or power, so saying it to someone's face can be insulting.

en: to be bereaved of; to be separated from someone by death

examples.en: My grandmother lost my grandfather a long time ago.

examples.ko: 젊은 나이에 남편과 사별해서 혼자 아이를 키웠어요.
examples.en: She lost her husband at a young age and raised the child alone.

examples.ko: 아내와 사별한 뒤 그분은 말수가 줄었어요.
examples.en: After losing his wife, that person spoke less.
When you lose your spouse, it is hard to pull yourself together.
Losing a family member is hard for anyone.
I heard the news that my friend lost their mother.

explain: '헤어지다'와 달리 죽음으로 이별했다는 뜻이 이 말에 들어 있어요. 주로 남편이나 아내에게 쓰고, 'A와 사별하다'처럼 '와/과'를 붙여요. 부모는 '여의다'를 더 자주 써요. 이혼은 '이혼하다'라고 해서 사별과 달라요.
explain_en: Unlike '헤어지다' (to part), this word itself carries the meaning that the parting was through death. It is mostly used for a husband or wife, in the pattern 'A와 사별하다'. For parents, '여의다' is more common. Divorce is '이혼하다', a different thing.

examples.ko: 생면부지의 사람이 길에서 제 짐을 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: A complete stranger helped carry my bags on the street.
I started living alone in a place where I knew no one.

examples.ko: 생면부지였던 두 사람이 이제는 가장 친한 친구예요.
examples.en: The two who were once total strangers are now the closest of friends.
I received help from a total stranger and tears came to my eyes.
I felt shy about asking a person I'd never met for directions.

examples.ko: 생면부지라서 처음엔 서로 말도 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: We were complete strangers, so at first we couldn't even speak to each other.

explain: 한 번도 만난 적 없는 사람뿐 아니라 '생면부지의 땅'처럼 처음 가 보는 곳에도 써요. '모르는 사람'보다 강조하는 느낌이 있고, 말보다는 글에서 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used not only for someone you have never met but also for a place you've never been, as in '생면부지의 땅'. It is stronger than '모르는 사람' (someone I don't know) and suits writing better than casual speech.

en: to cheer on; to support enthusiastically

examples.ko: 많은 분들이 우리 팀을 성원해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Many people cheered on our team.

examples.ko: 끝까지 성원해 주신 팬 여러분께 감사드려요.
examples.en: Thank you to the fans who supported us to the end.
The audience cheering for the athlete was moving.
I will keep supporting you as always.

examples.ko: 응원단이 큰 소리로 성원하자 선수들이 힘을 냈어요.
examples.en: When the cheering squad backed them loudly, the players found new energy.
Citizens eagerly backed the national team.

explain: '응원하다'보다 격식 있고 글이나 인사말에서 많이 써요. 보통 '성원해 주셔서 감사합니다'처럼 도와준 사람에게 고마움을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 가까운 사이의 일상 대화에서는 '응원해'라고 해요.
explain_en: More formal than '응원하다' and common in writing and greetings. You mostly hear it when thanking supporters, as in '성원해 주셔서 감사합니다'. In casual talk between close people, Koreans just say '응원해'.

examples.en: The kids are gathered together talking in whispers.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 수군수군 얘기하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear someone whispering behind me.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 수군수군 비밀 이야기를 나눠요.
examples.en: The two of them share secrets in whispers.
In the library, even whispers can be heard by everyone.
My friends were whispering and laughing next to me.

examples.ko: 수군수군 말하지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't whisper, speak up.

explain: '속닥속닥'처럼 작은 소리로 말하는 모양을 나타내는데, 여러 사람이 남 이야기를 하는 느낌이 있어요. 동사로는 '수군대다'를 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: Like '속닥속닥', it describes talking in low voices, but it often suggests several people talking about someone else. The matching verb is '수군대다'.

en: to talk in whispers; to talk low

examples.en: The villagers whispered to each other after hearing the rumor.
You shouldn't whisper during a meeting.
The two whispered something and then suddenly laughed.
I heard whispering in the hallway.

examples.ko: 내 앞에서 쑥덕거리지 말고 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't whisper in front of me; just tell me.

examples.ko: 이웃들이 새로 이사 온 집을 두고 쑥덕거려요.
examples.en: The neighbors are whispering about the family that just moved in.

explain: 소문이나 남의 흉을 몰래 주고받는 장면에 써서 부정적인 느낌이 강해요. 그냥 조용히 말하는 것은 '속삭이다'라고 해요. '쑤군거리다'와 바꿔 써도 돼요.
explain_en: It is used for secretly trading rumors or gossip about others, so it feels negative. Simply speaking quietly is '속삭이다'. You can swap it with '쑤군거리다'.

examples.en: That child is small but tough.
The little girl answered in a firm, spirited voice.
She may be short, but she works with grit.
That player fought hard and won the ball.
My younger brother stood up fiercely to his older brother.

examples.ko: 암팡진 성격 덕분에 어려움을 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to her gutsy personality, she overcame the hardship.

explain: 몸집은 작은데 야무지고 당찬 모습에 써요. '야무지다'와 비슷하지만 작은 몸에 비해 힘차다는 느낌이 더 있어요. '암팡지게 달려들다', '암팡진 목소리'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used for someone small in build but firm, capable and spirited. It is similar to '야무지다' but has more of a feeling of being strong for one's small size. Typical uses are '암팡지게 달려들다' and '암팡진 목소리'.

examples.ko: 얼간이 같은 실수를 해서 너무 부끄러워요.
examples.en: I made such a stupid mistake and I'm so embarrassed.

examples.ko: 그 얼간이가 비밀번호를 친구한테 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: That fool told his friend the password.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 얼간이는 아니지만 좀 느려요.
examples.en: He's not an idiot, but he's a bit slow.
Only I didn't know anything, like a fool.

examples.ko: 그렇게 쉬운 걸 틀리다니 제가 얼간이였어요.
examples.en: I got something that easy wrong. I was such an idiot.

examples.ko: 친구에게 얼간이라고 하면 싸울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you call a friend an idiot, you might end up fighting.

explain: 모자라고 어리숙한 사람을 낮잡아 부르는 말이라, 상대에게 직접 쓰면 모욕이 될 수 있어요. 친한 사이의 농담이나 자기 자신을 탓할 때 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 비슷한 말로 '바보', '멍청이'가 있어요.
explain_en: It looks down on someone who is foolish or easily fooled, so saying it directly to a person can be insulting. It is often used as a joke between close friends or to blame oneself. Similar words are '바보' and '멍청이'.

examples.en: The director of this drama is a famous filmmaker.
The director explained the scene to the actors.
A stage director is responsible for the whole stage.
The director and the actor talked for a long time.
It was hard to understand the director's intention.
The director received an award at the ceremony.

explain: 영화는 '감독'이라고 부르고, 연극이나 방송, 공연은 '연출자'나 '연출가'라는 말을 많이 써요. 방송에서는 PD가 연출자 역할을 하는 때가 많아요. '연출'은 장면을 짜고 배우를 이끄는 일을 가리켜요.
explain_en: For movies the usual word is 감독, while for plays, broadcasts and performances 연출자 or 연출가 is common. In broadcasting, a PD often plays the role of the 연출자. 연출 is the work of arranging the scenes and guiding the actors.

examples.en: The family gathers cozily and eats dinner.
The old couple chats warmly together.

examples.ko: 친구들과 오순도순 사는 게 제 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to live peacefully with my friends.
The brothers get along so well, which is nice to see.
The neighbors live sharing warm feelings with each other.
Let's get along nicely.

explain: 사이좋게 정답게 모여 지내거나 이야기하는 모습에 써요. 주로 가족, 이웃, 친구처럼 가까운 사람들에게 쓰고, 보통 '지내다, 살다, 이야기하다'와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It describes people getting along warmly, whether living together or talking. It is mostly used for close people like family, neighbors and friends, and usually goes with '지내다', '살다' and '이야기하다'.

examples.en: They say the famous writer passed away last night.
He passed away quietly in the hospital.
I wrote down the date he passed away in the book.
Before passing away, he left a letter for his family.

examples.ko: 삼 년 전에 운명한 시인의 시를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a poem by a poet who passed away three years ago.
Everyone was shocked at the news that he had passed away.

explain: '죽다'보다 아주 격식 있는 말이에요. 주로 신문 기사나 장례식 같은 자리에서 써요. 높일 때는 '돌아가시다'가 훨씬 더 일반적이니 일상에서는 '돌아가시다'를 쓰세요. 소리가 같은 '운명'(타고난 앞날)과 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: This is a very formal word for dying, mainly in newspaper articles and funeral settings. In daily life, '돌아가시다' is far more common when showing respect, so use that. Do not confuse it with the same-sounding '운명' (fate).

dis.h: literary: breathe one's last, moment of death

p.n: 돌아가시다 is the everyday polite way; 운명하다 sounds literary.

examples.en: The two of them are sworn brothers.
He cherishes his old friend like a brother.
It's already been twenty years since we became sworn brothers.
We promised to become sworn brothers.

examples.ko: 의형제 사이라 서로 속마음을 다 알아요.
examples.en: We're sworn brothers, so we know each other's real feelings.

examples.ko: 영화 속 의형제가 눈물 나게 했어요.
examples.en: The sworn brothers in the movie made me cry.

explain: 피가 섞이지 않았지만 형제처럼 지내기로 약속한 사이를 말해요. '의형제를 맺다'라는 표현으로 많이 써요. 실제 형제를 말하는 '친형제'와 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to people who aren't related by blood but have agreed to be like brothers. It is commonly used in the phrase '의형제를 맺다'. It differs from '친형제', which means real siblings.

en: to tell tales; to tattle; to tell on

examples.ko: 동생이 내가 몰래 과자를 먹었다고 엄마한테 일러바쳤어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling told on me to Mom for secretly eating the snacks.

examples.ko: 친구가 선생님께 내 실수를 일러바칠까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried my friend will tell the teacher about my mistake.

examples.ko: 일러바치지 말고 직접 말해 보는 게 어때요?
examples.en: Instead of tattling, why don't you tell them directly?

examples.ko: 누가 일러바쳤는지 모르겠지만 사장님이 알고 계셨어요.
examples.en: I don't know who told on me, but the boss already knew.

examples.ko: 그 애는 툭하면 일러바쳐서 친구들이 싫어해요.
examples.en: That kid tattles at the drop of a hat, so the other kids dislike him.

examples.ko: 몰래 한 일을 아빠에게 일러바치다니 너무해요.
examples.en: I can't believe you told Dad about what I did in secret. That's so mean!

explain: '고자질하다'와 비슷한 뜻이지만 '일러바치다'가 더 입말 느낌이고 아이들 이야기에서 자주 보여요. 주로 윗사람에게 남의 잘못을 알리는 일이라 비난하는 느낌이 들어요.
explain_en: It is close to '고자질하다' but sounds more colloquial and often appears in talk about kids. It usually means reporting someone's wrongdoing to an authority figure, so it carries a tone of disapproval.
